newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade at higher levels.

text.p: German shares took their cue from Wall Street and the dollar early on Thursday and posted solid gains over bourse trade, but dealers said ongoing uncertainty about European monetary union capped the market's advance.
"We are delighted to see the market getting back in step with Wall Street," said one Frankfurt dealer.
"All in all we have a strong operating environment and the dollar is adding some extra pep," said a Munich trader.
The 30-share DAX index ended up 30.56 points, or 0.83 percent, at 3,707.99 points in the first half hour of trade, having vaulted the key hurdle of 3,700 points early in the session.
"If we don't get a clear message from (Finance Minister Theo) Waigel and (Bundesbank President Hans) Tietmeyer today, this will still be a nervous market," said a dealer.

The plans triggered an unprecedented dispute between Bonn and the central bank, which viewed an original proposal to use the revaluation proceeds to help Germany meet Maastricht deficit goals as unacceptable.
The Bundesbank did not include a statement on the issue in its regular post-meeting statement, and market players did not entirely rule out a statement later on.

All 30 German blue chips rose moderately after the Dow Jones' ascent to its fourth consecutive record close while the dollar firmed to trade at 1.725 against the mark -- always a good signal for Germany's dollar-sensitive exporters.

The chief underperformer was chemicals and pharmaceuticals group Altana AG after it issued a statement late on Wednesday countering market rumours that it was either to be taken over or planned to launch a new drug in the U.S. soon.
Altana shares, which surged on Wednesday, ended bourse trade down 4.76 percent at 1,700 marks.
Share prices were also being influenced by next week's expiry of DAX options contracts on the DTB exchange, which always causes fluctuations on the cash market.
Dealers said the most actively traded option aimed for a strike price of 3,700 DAX points.
